lines.text: A Roman cup glows red when backlit.
The Lycurgus Cup is a Roman glass cup from the 4th century.
lines.say: The ly-KUR-gus Cup is a Roman glass cup from the fourth century.

lines.text: Lit from the front, it looks opaque green.
Shine light through from behind and the glass glows red.
Tiny gold and silver specks in the glass cause the change.
The specks are around 50 to 100 nanometers across.
lines.say: The specks are around fifty to one hundred nanometers across.

lines.text: That is over 1,000 times smaller than a grain of table salt.
lines.say: That is over one thousand times smaller than a grain of table salt.

lines.text: Most experts think its figures were cut from a thick glass blank.
The figures show King Lycurgus caught in grapevine tendrils.
lines.say: The figures show King ly-KUR-gus caught in grapevine tendrils.

lines.text: The British Museum bought it from the Rothschild family in 1958.
lines.say: The British Museum bought it from the ROTHS-child family in nineteen fifty eight.

Shine light through from behind and the glass glows red. Tiny gold and silver specks in the glass cause the change. The specks are around 50 to 100 nanometers across. That is over 1,000 times smaller than a grain of table salt. Most experts think its figures were cut from a thick glass blank. The figures show King Lycurgus caught in grapevine tendrils.
